name: JTBD switch interview
description: Reconstruct a real purchase or switch decision on a timeline to learn what actually drives adoption.
promptDelta:
Restructure the script as a Jobs-to-be-Done switch interview about a recent purchase or switch the participant actually made.
- Screen for people who bought or switched within the last 3–6 months.
- Walk the timeline: first thought, passive looking, active looking, deciding, first use, ongoing use.
- At each step, probe the four forces: push of the old situation, pull of the new solution, anxiety about switching, habit of the present.
- Ask about specific moments ("Tell me about the last time ..."), not opinions or hypotheticals.
- Add a timeline and forces diagram to the synthesis template.

name: Problem discovery (no pitching)
description: Validate that the problem is real and costly before showing any solution, using past behavior rather than opinions.
promptDelta:
Run this as problem-discovery interviewing:
- Do not describe or pitch our product or any solution idea during the interview.
- Ask about past behavior and specifics, not future intentions. Avoid "Would you ...?" and "Do you think ...?".
- For each theme, ask how they handle it today, what it costs them (time, money, workarounds) and what they have already tried.
- Add a "commitment signals" row to the synthesis template (for example an intro to a colleague, agreeing to a pilot, sharing data) to separate real interest from compliments.

name: Concept & usability test
description: Pair a short discovery warm-up with task-based testing of a prototype or concept.
promptDelta:
Turn the session into a concept and usability test.
- Keep discovery questions to about the first quarter of the session, then show the prototype or concept.
- Write 3–5 task scenarios tied to the key themes, each with a success criterion.
- Use think-aloud and neutral probes ("What would you expect to happen?"), never "Do you like it?".
- Add a task table (Task | Success criterion | Observed | Severity) to the synthesis template, and a preparation checklist (prototype link, recording consent, test data).

name: B2B multi-stakeholder
description: For B2B products where users, buyers and admins are different people with different concerns.
promptDelta:
Adapt the guide for B2B interviews where users, buyers and admins may be different people.
- Add screener questions that identify the participant's role in purchasing and in day-to-day use.
- Give each role its own question track: workflow pain for users; business case, budget and procurement for buyers; setup, security and integrations for admins.
- Add questions about how a tool like this gets approved in their organization.
- Remind the interviewer not to ask for confidential data and to check whether the participant needs their company's permission to take part.
